# planar.library: Perimeter

**Status:** Supported (tier `geometry`). In a shipping tier; the lint, type-check, and code-generation gates cover it. No release promises its signature yet.

## Summary

### Law_SuperEllipseExponentTwoPerimeterIsEllipse

[stdlib/tests/special-numerics.laws.plato, line 99](../../../../../stdlib/tests/special-numerics.laws.plato#L99)

```plato
// At Exponent 2 the superellipse IS the ellipse, so its numerically integrated
// perimeter must match the ellipse's.
//
// TOLERANCE: set by the WEAKER of the two sides, which is the ellipse. Its
// Perimeter is Ramanujan's second approximation, whose relative error is not
// symmetric in the axis ratio: it is below 1e-9 for b/a >= 0.4 but grows to
// -1.2e-5 at b/a = 0.1 and to -4.0e-4 in the degenerate limit b/a -> 0
// (measured against a converged arc-length integral). The Simpson integral on
// the superellipse side tracks the true perimeter to float32 precision
// (~4e-7 relative), so 1e-3 is the tightest tolerance this identity supports
// over the whole semi-axis regime, where b/a reaches 0.001. Do not read it as
// the accuracy of either body; the guard is the ellipse approximation, and
// tightening it means improving Ellipse.Perimeter (tracked, see plato-373).
Law_SuperEllipseExponentTwoPerimeterIsEllipse(se: SuperEllipse): Boolean
    => se.SuperEllipseOutOfRegime
    || SuperEllipse(se.Center, se.SemiAxes, se.Rotation, 2.0).Perimeter
        .SpecialEqWithin(Ellipse(se.Center, se.SemiAxes, se.Rotation).Perimeter,
                         1e-3);
```

### Law_SuperEllipseExponentOnePerimeterIsDiamond

[stdlib/tests/special-numerics.laws.plato, line 107](../../../../../stdlib/tests/special-numerics.laws.plato#L107)

```plato
// At Exponent 1 the superellipse is the diamond with vertices on the axes,
// whose perimeter is exactly 4 sqrt(a^2 + b^2).
Law_SuperEllipseExponentOnePerimeterIsDiamond(se: SuperEllipse): Boolean
    => se.SuperEllipseOutOfRegime
    || SuperEllipse(se.Center, se.SemiAxes, se.Rotation, 1.0).Perimeter
        .SpecialEq(4.0 * (se.SemiAxes.X.Square + se.SemiAxes.Y.Square).Sqrt);
```

### Law_SuperEllipseUnitCirclePerimeter

[stdlib/tests/special-numerics.laws.plato, line 114](../../../../../stdlib/tests/special-numerics.laws.plato#L114)

```plato
// The unit circle as a superellipse (a = b = 1, Exponent 2) has perimeter
// 2 pi.
Law_SuperEllipseUnitCirclePerimeter(t: Number): Boolean
    => SuperEllipse(Point2D.Origin, Number2.One, Angle(0.0), 2.0)
        .Perimeter.SpecialEq(Number.Tau);
```

### Line 55

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/planar.library.plato, line 55](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/planar.library.plato#L55).

```plato

    // The four straight runs (2(w + h) - 8r) plus the four quarter arcs (2*pi*r).
    Perimeter(r: RoundedRect2D): Number
    {
        var radius = r.EffectiveCornerRadius;
        return 2.0 * (r.Rect.Size.Width + r.Rect.Size.Height)
            - 8.0 * radius + 2.0 * Number.Pi * radius;
    }
```

```plato
    Perimeter(a: Annulus): Number
        => 2.0 * Number.Pi * (a.OuterRadius + a.InnerRadius);
```

### Line 459

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/planar.library.plato, line 459](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/planar.library.plato#L459).

```plato

    // APPROXIMATE. The circumference of an ellipse is a complete elliptic integral
    // of the second kind and has NO elementary closed form; this is RAMANUJAN'S
    // SECOND APPROXIMATION,
    //     P ~= pi (a + b) (1 + 3h / (10 + sqrt(4 - 3h))),  h = ((a-b)/(a+b))^2,
    // which is exact for a circle (h = 0) and degrades monotonically with
    // eccentricity: the worst case is the fully degenerate ellipse b = 0, where it
    // returns (14/11)*pi*a = 3.99838*a against the true 4*a — a relative error of
    // -4.0e-4. MEASURED against a converged arc-length integral, the relative error
    // is -4.6e-10 at b/a = 0.5, -6.3e-9 at b/a = 0.4, -7.4e-8 at b/a = 0.3,
    // -1.2e-5 at b/a = 0.1 and -3.8e-4 at b/a = 0.001. So "below 1e-8" holds only
    // for b/a >= 0.4; do not assume this body is accurate for flattened ellipses.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellipse#Circumference
    Perimeter(e: Ellipse): Number
    {
        var a = e.SemiAxes.X;
        var b = e.SemiAxes.Y;
        var h = ((a - b) / (a + b)).Square;
        return Number.Pi * (a + b) * (1.0 + 3.0 * h / (10.0 + (4.0 - 3.0 * h).Sqrt));
    }
```

### Line 566

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/planar.library.plato, line 566](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/planar.library.plato#L566).

```plato

    // APPROXIMATE. The superellipse perimeter has NO closed form for general n;
    // this is a numerical arc-length integral: each quarter splits at the diagonal
    // point (x/a)^n = 1/2 into two graph segments (one per axis, the second by
    // symmetry with a and b swapped), each integrated by 96-panel Simpson, times 4.
    // Precondition: Exponent >= 1 (see the integrand). Verified accuracy: n = 2
    // reproduces the ellipse to ~2e-9 relative; ~5e-8 at n = 4, ~6e-7 at n = 8,
    // degrading to ~1e-4 by n = 50 as the shape forms corners.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superellipse
    Perimeter(se: SuperEllipse): Number
        => 4.0 * (SuperEllipseArcSegment(se.SemiAxes.X, se.SemiAxes.Y, se.Exponent)
                + SuperEllipseArcSegment(se.SemiAxes.Y, se.SemiAxes.X, se.Exponent));
```
